newsitem.title: USA: Navistar sees lower industry truck demand.
newsitem.headline: Navistar sees lower industry truck demand.

text.p: Navistar International Inc said Wednesday it expects industry demand for heavy trucks in the United States and Canada will reach 170,000 units in 1997, down 13 percent from 195,400 heavy trucks sold by the industry in 1996.
Navistar also said it expects industry demand for medium trucks in the United States and Canada will reach 112,000 units in 1997, a slight decrease from the 113,200 trucks sold in 1996.
Navistar said it forecasts industry demand for school buses in fiscal 1997 will remain relatively flat compared with the 32,500 buses sold in 1996.
Navistar makes heavy and medium trucks and school buses and also manufactures mid-range diesel engines.

Earlier, Navistar reported a net loss of $0.10 a share for the fourth quarter ended October 31, compared with year-ago earnings of $0.66 a share. Total sales and revenues for the quarter fell to $1.45 billion from $1.77 billion.
For fiscal 1996, it had a profit of $0.49 a share, compared with a year-ago profit of $1.83.
Total sales and revenues for the year were $5.75 billion, down from $6.34 billion.

"While our results can be attributed to a downturn in the industry, our performance last year was not acceptable," John Horne, chairman, said. "We now are executing strategies to retool those businesses where performance is lacking and to grow those where we're gaining competitive advantages."

Navistar said its worldwide shipments of 95,200 medium and heavy trucks and school buses during fiscal 1996 were 15 percent lower than a year ago. Shipments of mid-range diesel engines during the year totaled a record 163,200 units, a six percent rise from last year. Sales of service parts rose four percent to $760.0 million.

Navistar said it maintained its position as the sales leader in the U.S. and Canadian retail markets for heavy and medium trucks and school buses, achieving a 27.5 percent market share, up 0.8 points from a year ago.
